zta-free-asset-factory.name: elevated_road_support_a_v01
zta-free-asset-factory.description: A tall engineered support assembly for TechTown's elevated vehicle lanes. It begins with a wide reinforced concrete crash footing and rises through a tapered composite-clad pier with a recessed inspection door, drainage outlet, service conduit, and protected maintenance ladder. A broad transverse cap beam at the top carries four replaceable elastomeric bearing pads, two lateral restraint blocks, expansion-joint catch trays, and visible bolted access plates beneath the roadway deck. Diagonal steel knee braces connect the pier to the cap beam and create a recognizable load path instead of leaving a slab floating on a column. Low collision guards and reflective hazard bands protect the base at street level. Controlled cyan inspection lights may accent access points, but the structure remains primarily concrete, dark metal, and black composite.

zta-free-asset-factory.name: gap-aqualume-airlock-conduit-straight-standard-105
zta-free-asset-factory.description: A straight enclosed connector for joining dry Aqualume interiors across wet exterior space. The primary form is a thick pressure-glass pedestrian tube running between two oversized circular docking collars. Each end has layered compression flanges, visible gasket seams, locking dogs, alignment keys, and a short reinforced transition throat that can mate cleanly with neighboring modules. Five external load-bearing pressure hoops wrap the span and connect to a lower service spine carrying current cables, drainage, oxygen lines, and inspection access. One side includes a recessed service hatch with latch hardware, pressure gauge, warning placard, and emergency isolation valve. A narrow illuminated floor strip and repeated directional icons preserve orientation without relying on color alone. The conduit must read as hollow traversable architecture with believable wall thickness, not a solid cylinder or a rectangular bridge wearing round end caps.
